Subject: Onramp allocator approval and OEM queue triage

Team,

We reached a contract agreement in principle with Acme (deal id ACME-DEAL-2027-11) and they want a firm onramp window to hit production by mid-November. The sizing worksheet attached shows a 1.5M RU quarter and an initial dedicated pool request for 48 x A100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state 32, burst to 48) with a small staging pool for warmups and evals.

Action items I need aligned this week:
- NVIDIA: please confirm the OEM quote line items in OEM_quote_NV-RTX-7000.pdf and provide a committed ETA range (earliest/likely/latest) for the 48-unit tranche. We need manufacturing/ship window + estimated customs lead time.
- PaloCloud: confirm whether we can reserve a guaranteed 48-GPU cloud lane for the 90-day onboarding window, or provide a documented fallback (burstable across regions) and pricing delta.
- Acme: confirm that the proposed acceptance criteria (latency p95, throughput, and storage retention) in the attached sizing sheet work for you, or flag any procurement gating items.

I'm copying Ben and Karthik for capacity allocation and Vanessa for staging-pool layout. Rishi — please review the fallback economics if OEM is delayed.

Attachments: Acme_DEAL_Sizing_Reqs_v2.xlsx; OEM_quote_NV-RTX-7000.pdf; staging-pool-layout-v1.png

Thanks,
Monica

Subject: Re: Onramp allocator approval and OEM queue triage

Monica / team,

Thanks for the details and the workbook — helpful. Quick summary from our side:
- SKU confirmation: the quote reflects 48x NV-RTX-7000-class boards (part #NV-7000-BUNDLE). Pricing in OEM_quote_NV-RTX-7000.pdf is correct for standard commercial terms.
- ETA window: earliest ship: 2027-09-20; likely ship: 2027-10-12; latest: 2027-11-03. These ranges assume current queue positions and no custom manufacturing change requests.
- Customs / transit: add ~7-14 days for cross-border shipment to the West Coast fulfillment center; ports/slots can fluctuate.
- Ramp advice: if Acme wants a hard Nov 15 production, we consider the Oct 12 likely ship as borderline safe, but recommend a 2-week buffer for staging and QoS tuning.

We can offer a 'priority lane' for an expedite fee (2.5% premium) that shifts the likely ship earlier by ~10 days, conditional on a non-refundable deposit to secure a manufacturing slot.

I'll attach the formal ETA confirmation and revised quote if you want me to proceed.

Regards,
Lina Gomez
Enterprise Accounts, NVIDIA OEM
enterprise@nvidia.com

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp allocator approval and OEM queue triage

Hi Monica / team,

We can provision a reserved 48-GPU lane in our US-west region for the requested onboarding window. Two notes:
1) Reserved pool vs burst: a guaranteed dedicated pool requires a 6-week lead to reserve capacity on our staging cluster and a 3-month minimum commitment. If you need a shorter window we can do a hybrid reservation (32 guaranteed + 16 burstable) with a modest uplift.
2) Networking / colo: to meet the acceptance p95 latency target with Acme's traffic profile you should target colocated interconnects — I see Vanessa's staging diagram, that's helpful.

Pricing summary: guaranteed 48 (90-day): $78k/month; hybrid 32g guarantee + 16 burst: $62k/month. We offer a credit if OEM ship slips and you route to our burst lane.

If you want to lock a guaranteed lane we'll need confirmation by Jul 23 and a signed MSA addendum.

Best,
Tom Aldridge
Head of Partnerships, PaloCloud
sales@palocloud.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onramp allocator approval and OEM queue triage

Monica / team — quick internal alignment and rec to Acme:

- Recommendation: accept NVIDIA's 'likely' ship scenario (2027-10-12) as baseline but require vendor-confirmed expedite option (2.5% fee) in writing. That gives us a contract lever if Acme needs an earlier hard date.
- PaloCloud: push for hybrid reservation (32 guaranteed + 16 burst) as the default to reduce committed spend and preserve operational flexibility. We'll take the credit clause if the OEM slips.
- Procurement ask to Acme: confirm your internal cutover freeze window for schema/keys and whether we can use a partial cutover (service-by-service) to reduce the end-to-end staging time.

I'll draft the mutual action plan (MAP) with timeline buckets (procure sign, OEM deposit opt-in, PaloCloud reservation, staging run, go/no-go gate). Monica — can you nudge Acme procurement for freeze-window and contract signature timeline?

Ben
Ben Carter

Ben / Monica / team,

Thanks for the clear plan. Procurement confirms:
- Acme internal freeze window target: 01-Nov-2027 to 15-Nov-2027 for phased production cutover. We can do a rolling service cutover starting Nov 8 if the hardware arrives early and Redwood certs staging.
- We're comfortable with the hybrid PaloCloud reservation, pending the credit clause for OEM slips.
- We'll review the NVIDIA expedite option this week and confirm whether we can approve a deposit.

Please send the MAP and the updated vendor-side SLA language for our legal review. We should aim to sign the MSA addendum by Jul 23 to preserve PaloCloud's reservation ability.

Regards,
Maya Patel
